meta.name: Manage LinkedIn posts and engagement with an MCP server and AI agents

name: LinkedIn MCP Server – Post, Engage & Manage with Your AI Agent

parameters.content:
## LinkedIn MCP Server – Post, Engage & Manage with Your AI Agent

### How it works

This workflow exposes a full LinkedIn toolkit through an **MCP Server Trigger** so any MCP-compatible AI agent (Claude, Cursor, an n8n AI Agent, etc.) can call actions on demand: create text / image / article posts, read your profile and recent posts, edit or delete a post, and comment on, react to, or moderate engagement. The agent picks the right tool and arguments — you don't run this workflow manually. Every LinkedIn node reads a single `linkedin_person_urn` Variable, so there's nothing to find-and-replace.

### Setup

1. Create a **LinkedIn OAuth2** credential (enable the *Share on LinkedIn* and *Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect* products in your LinkedIn Developer app) and select it on every LinkedIn node.
2. Create a **Bearer Auth** credential for the MCP Server Trigger, and use the same token in your AI client's MCP configuration.
3. In **n8n Settings → Variables**, add `linkedin_person_urn` and set it to your LinkedIn person ID (call the *Fetch LinkedIn Profile* tool once to find it). Every tool depends on this — without it, calls send an empty URN and LinkedIn rejects them.
4. Copy the MCP Server Trigger's **Production URL** into your MCP client so it can call these tools.
5. For image posts, make sure your MCP client sends the image as binary data and pass the correct binary field name to the image-post tool.

### Customization

Adjust tool names, descriptions, and parameters to match how your agent should invoke LinkedIn actions, and add safeguards around destructive tools (delete post, delete comment, remove reaction). Want post analytics or company-page posting? Both need LinkedIn's Marketing Developer Platform approval — add an organization URN Variable once approved.

## ⚠️ Set your Variable first

Before using any tool, create the `linkedin_person_urn` Variable in **Settings → Variables** and set it to your LinkedIn person ID. Every node reads it — if it's missing, calls send an empty/undefined URN and LinkedIn rejects them. Run **Fetch LinkedIn Profile** once to retrieve your ID.

## Server and profile access

Hosts the MCP entry point for the AI agent and provides a nearby profile lookup tool for retrieving the authenticated LinkedIn user's profile details.

## Author feed and text posts

A far-left cluster for retrieving recent posts by an author and creating plain text LinkedIn updates.

## Post lookup and deletion

A nearby post-management cluster for fetching a specific LinkedIn post and deleting a LinkedIn post when requested.

## Publish and engage content

A right-side cluster that publishes image or article-link updates and handles engagement actions such as commenting, listing comments, and reacting to posts.

## Update and moderate activity

A lower cluster for maintaining existing LinkedIn activity, including deleting comments, removing reactions, getting reaction data, and updating posts.

parameters.text: ={{ /*n8n-auto-generated-fromAI-override*/ $fromAI('Text', `The full text content of the post, exactly as it should appear. Preserve the user's voice; don't invent hashtags unless asked.`, 'string') }}
parameters.toolDescription: Publish a plain text update to LinkedIn with no image or link attachment. Use this for text-only posts: announcements, opinions, short updates. Do not use if the user wants to attach an image or share a link with a preview — use the image or article tool instead.

parameters.text: ={{ /*n8n-auto-generated-fromAI-override*/ $fromAI('Text', `The caption text to accompany the image.`, 'string') }}
parameters.toolDescription: Publish a LinkedIn post that includes a single image attachment. Use this when the user wants to share a post together with an image that is already available as binary data on the input. Do not use if there is no image to attach — use the text or article tool instead.

additionalFields.title: ={{ /*n8n-auto-generated-fromAI-override*/ $fromAI('Title', `Optional short title displayed with the image.`, 'string') }}

parameters.binaryPropertyName: ={{ /*n8n-auto-generated-fromAI-override*/ $fromAI('Input_Binary_Field', `Name of the binary property holding the image file to attach (typically "data").`, 'string') }}

parameters.text: ={{ /*n8n-auto-generated-fromAI-override*/ $fromAI('Text', `The commentary/caption text to accompany the shared article link.`, 'string') }}
parameters.toolDescription: Publish a LinkedIn post that shares an external link (article, blog post, webpage) with LinkedIn's own link preview. Use this when the user wants to share a URL, not attach an image directly. Do not use for plain text-only updates or image posts.

additionalFields.description: ={{ /*n8n-auto-generated-fromAI-override*/ $fromAI('Description', `The commentary/caption text to accompany the shared article link.`, 'string') }}
additionalFields.originalUrl: ={{ /*n8n-auto-generated-fromAI-override*/ $fromAI('Original_URL', `The full URL of the article or webpage to share.`, 'string') }}

parameters.toolDescription: Fetch the most recent posts published by the connected LinkedIn account, sorted by last modified. Use this to check what's already been posted, avoid duplicate content, or reference a recent post. Returns up to 10 posts. Does not accept a query — always returns the latest posts for this account.

parameters.url: ={{ 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/posts/' + encodeURIComponent($fromAI('Post_URN', 'The full LinkedIn post URN to fetch, e.g. urn:li:share:7123456789012345678', 'string')) }}
parameters.toolDescription: Fetch full details of one specific LinkedIn post by its URN. Use this when the user references a specific post (e.g. after listing recent posts) and needs its full content, not just a summary.

parameters.url: ={{ 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/posts/' + encodeURIComponent($fromAI('Post_URN', 'The full LinkedIn post URN to delete, e.g. urn:li:share:7123456789012345678', 'string')) }}
parameters.toolDescription: Permanently delete a LinkedIn post by its URN. This is irreversible — only call this when the user has explicitly confirmed they want a specific post deleted. Never call this speculatively or as a "cleanup" step without direct instruction.
Fetch the profile of the currently connected LinkedIn account (name, headline, person ID). Use this to confirm which account is connected, or to find the person URN needed for other tools.

parameters.url: ={{ 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/socialActions/' + encodeURIComponent($fromAI('Post_URN', 'The LinkedIn post URN to comment on, e.g. urn:li:share:7123456789012345678', 'string')) + '/comments' }}
parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { actor: 'urn:li:person:' + $vars.linkedin_person_urn, message: { text: $fromAI('Comment_Text', 'the comment text to post', 'string') } } }}
parameters.toolDescription: Post a comment on an existing LinkedIn post. Use this when the user wants to engage with a specific post rather than create a new one.

parameters.url: ={{ 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/socialActions/' + encodeURIComponent($fromAI('Post_URN', 'The LinkedIn post URN to fetch comments for, e.g. urn:li:share:7123456789012345678', 'string')) + '/comments' }}
parameters.toolDescription: Fetch the existing comments on a specific LinkedIn post. Use this to review engagement or check what's already been said before commenting or reacting.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { root: $fromAI('Post_URN', 'the LinkedIn post URN to react to, e.g. urn:li:share:7123456789012345678', 'string'), reactionType: $fromAI('Reaction_Type', 'one of LIKE, PRAISE, APPRECIATION, EMPATHY, INTEREST, ENTERTAINMENT', 'string') } }}
parameters.toolDescription: Add a reaction (like, praise, etc.) to a specific LinkedIn post. Use this for lightweight engagement instead of writing a comment.

parameters.url: ={{ 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/socialActions/' + encodeURIComponent($fromAI('Post_URN', 'The LinkedIn post URN the comment belongs to, formatted like urn:li:share:7123456789012345678 or urn:li:ugcPost:7123456789012345678. Get this from context or from a prior Get posts/comments call — never invent it.', 'string')) + '/comments/' + encodeURIComponent($fromAI('Comment_Id', 'The numeric id of the comment to delete, exactly as returned in the "id" field by the Get comments on a LinkedIn post tool. Do not guess this value.', 'string')) }}
parameters.toolDescription: Permanently deletes one comment from a LinkedIn post. Use this only when the user explicitly asks to remove/delete a comment they left. You need the comment's numeric ID — if you don't already have it, call 'Get comments on a LinkedIn post' first to find it. This cannot be undone.

parameters.url: ={{ 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/reactions/(actor:' + encodeURIComponent('urn:li:person:' + $vars.linkedin_person_urn) + ',entity:' + encodeURIComponent($fromAI('Post_URN', 'The LinkedIn post URN to remove your reaction from, formatted like urn:li:share:7123456789012345678. Get this from context or a prior tool call.', 'string')) + ')' }}
parameters.toolDescription: Removes (un-reacts / unlikes) the reaction that the connected LinkedIn account previously left on a post. Use this when the user wants to undo a like or reaction they already added — not for removing someone else's reaction, which the API does not allow. Only needs the post URN.

parameters.url: ={{ 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/socialActions/' + encodeURIComponent($fromAI('Post_URN', 'The LinkedIn post URN to fetch reactions for, formatted like urn:li:share:7123456789012345678.', 'string')) + '/reactions' }}
parameters.toolDescription: Fetches the list of reactions on a LinkedIn post — who reacted and which reaction type (LIKE, PRAISE, APPRECIATION, EMPATHY, INTEREST, ENTERTAINMENT) they used. Use this when the user asks who engaged with a post, wants an engagement summary, or wants reaction counts. This only returns reactions, not comments — use 'Get comments on a LinkedIn post' for those.

parameters.url: ={{ 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/posts/' + encodeURIComponent($fromAI('Post_URN', 'The full LinkedIn post URN to edit, formatted like urn:li:share:7123456789012345678.', 'string')) }}
parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { patch: { '$set': { commentary: $fromAI('New_Text', 'The full replacement text for the post. This is not appended — it completely replaces the existing commentary, so include the entire new wording, not just the changed part.', 'string') } } } }}
parameters.toolDescription: Edits the text of a LinkedIn post you already published, without deleting and recreating it (so comments, reactions, and the URN stay intact). Use this when the user wants to fix a typo or reword an existing post. Requires the full replacement text — always ask for or assemble the complete new wording, since this replaces the entire commentary, not just a snippet.
